title: Southern Syncopators members; Sidney Spies and Dutch Flick
summary: Members of the five-piece band (Ferriot, Jelpe, Spies, Dutch Flick), the Music Box dance hall and Flick's later life.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who else were in the Southern Syncopators with you?

Um, we didn't have a bass player. We had a banjo player by the name of Henry Ferriot. We had a saxophone player by the name of John Jelpe. There was a Dr. Jelpe who was a famous doctor in New Orleans.

No. Maybe so. All probability, yeah. Could be. And, uh, Sidney Spies was on trumpet. Sidney was on, this was on, we were all union players, I think in those days. Yeah. Yeah. We were union then. And, uh, Sidney Spies was a trumpet player. He worked, I remember he worked out at the music box when I was there. It was a dance hall down on Canal and, Canal and Cronlette on the second floor. Diamond Dance deal. We had three piano players in there. We mentioned that the last time.
Yeah, we did, but we didn't get the rest of the band, so it kept going.

And, uh, Sidney Spies and, uh, only a five-piece band. And I was playing piano. Piano, drums, Dutch Flick, Roland Flick. Flick. You know that name familiar? His son was the head of the Ford Motor Company, something, you know, down here in New Orleans. But Flick, Dutch was, he fixed, he fixed Eddie Miller's Ford before Eddie Miller went to New York. So he could, it would get him there. Uh, he, Roland was, he, he went into the sort of antique business. And, uh, oddly enough, I bought a piece of property over there on Cuyosa and Bienville. And now my place is right here and right across the street was his house.
